list_bots.title: List bots
list_bots.description: List every bot in the BotStar account the access token belongs to, with each bot's id and name. Start here: almost every other tool takes a bot_id.

output.description: An array of bots. Each item has: id, name, team_name.

create_bot.title: Create bot
create_bot.description: Create a new, empty bot in the account and return it with its id. Build its content in the BotStar editor or through the CMS and attribute tools, then publish_bot to take it live.

get_bot.title: Get bot
get_bot.description: Read one bot by id: its name, languages and configuration.

output.description: A bot info: id, name, team_name.

list_bot_attributes.title: List bot attributes
list_bot_attributes.description: List a bot's attributes: the bot-wide variables (name, data type, value, and per-language values on a multilingual bot) that flows can read.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to read: `draft` (the editable version) or `live` (the published one). Omit for the provider default.

output.description: Default Response. Each item has: id, name, desc, value, value_..., data_type.

create_bot_attribute.title: Create bot attribute
create_bot_attribute.description: Create a bot attribute, a bot-wide variable that flows can read. On a multilingual bot, give each language its own value with `value_<lang>` keys, e.g. {value: 'Hello', value_es: 'Hola'}.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

attribute.description: The attribute: {name, desc, data_type (string, number or date), value}. A date value is YYYY-MM-DD. Add `value_<lang>` keys for per-language values on a multilingual bot.

update_bot_attribute.title: Update bot attribute
update_bot_attribute.description: Change a bot attribute's description or value. On a multilingual bot, set per-language values with `value_<lang>` keys, e.g. {value: 'Hello', value_es: 'Hola'}.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

attribute.description: The fields to change: {desc, value}, plus `value_<lang>` keys for per-language values on a multilingual bot.

delete_bot_attribute.title: Delete bot attribute
delete_bot_attribute.description: Permanently delete a bot attribute. Flows that still reference it will read an empty value.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

publish_bot.title: Publish bot
publish_bot.description: Publish a bot's draft to live, so the changes made in the draft start serving real conversations immediately.

get_user.title: Get user
get_user.description: Read one chat user (audience member) of a bot: profile fields such as first_name, last_name, email, gender, plus the custom user attributes set for them.

otn_topics.description: Each item has: id, name, expired_at, token.

update_user_attributes.title: Update user attributes
update_user_attributes.description: Set attributes on a chat user: the built-in first_name, last_name, email, gender and birthday, and any custom user attribute already defined on the bot (create_user_attributes defines new ones).

attributes.description: Attribute values to set, at least one: first_name, last_name, email, gender (male, female or empty), birthday (YYYY-MM-DD), and any custom user attribute by its field name.

create_user_attributes.title: Create user attributes
create_user_attributes.description: Define a new custom user attribute on a bot, so that update_user_attributes and flows can store a value under it for each user.

list_cms_entities.title: List cms entities
list_cms_entities.description: List the CMS entities of a bot. An entity is a content collection (for example Products or FAQs) with typed fields and items that flows can query.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to read: `draft` (the editable version) or `live` (the published one). Omit for the provider default.

output.description: Get all entities response data. Each item has: id, name, fields.

create_cms_entity.title: Create cms entity
create_cms_entity.description: Create a CMS entity (a content collection) on a bot, optionally with its fields in the same call.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

fields.description: Each item has: unique_name, name, data_type, options.
Each item has: unique_name, name, data_type, options.

get_cms_entity.title: Get cms entity
get_cms_entity.description: Read one CMS entity: its name and the definition of each of its fields.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to read: `draft` (the editable version) or `live` (the published one). Omit for the provider default.

fields.description: Each item has: unique_name, name, data_type, options.

update_cms_entity.title: Update cms entity
update_cms_entity.description: Rename a CMS entity. Use the entity-field tools to change its fields.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

delete_cms_entity.title: Delete cms entity
delete_cms_entity.description: Permanently delete a CMS entity together with all of its fields and items.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

create_cms_entity_fields.title: Create cms entity fields
create_cms_entity_fields.description: Add one or more fields to a CMS entity. Each field has a unique_name, a display name and a data_type such as text, multiple_values or single_option (which takes options.predefined_data).

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

fields.description: Fields to add, each {unique_name, name, data_type}; a single_option field also takes options: {predefined_data: [{value, label}]}.

update_cms_entity_fields.title: Update cms entity fields
update_cms_entity_fields.description: Change one or more existing fields of a CMS entity, each addressed by its unique_name.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

fields.description: Fields to change, each {unique_name, name, ...}; unique_name says which field.

delete_cms_entity_fields.title: Delete cms entity fields
delete_cms_entity_fields.description: Permanently remove fields from a CMS entity, along with the values every item holds for them.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

unique_names.description: The list of Entity field unique_names

list_cms_entity_items.title: List cms entity items
list_cms_entity_items.description: List the items of a CMS entity, a page at a time, optionally filtered by name or status. Each item carries a value for every field of the entity.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to read: `draft` (the editable version) or `live` (the published one). Omit for the provider default.

limit.description: The numbers of items to return.

output.description: Get all entity items response data. Each item has: id, name, status, entity_id, field_unique_name1, field_unique_name2.

create_cms_entity_item.title: Create cms entity item
create_cms_entity_item.description: Add an item to a CMS entity. Besides name and status, the item takes one key per entity field, keyed by the field's unique_name.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

item.description: The item: {name (required), status (enabled or disabled)}, plus one key per entity field keyed by its unique_name; a multiple-values field takes an array. E.g. {name: 'Summer Polo Shirt', status: 'enabled', color: ['red','yellow'], price: '$10'}.

output.description: Create an entity item response data

get_cms_entity_item.title: Get cms entity item
get_cms_entity_item.description: Read one item of a CMS entity, with its value for each field.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to read: `draft` (the editable version) or `live` (the published one). Omit for the provider default.

output.description: Get an entity item response data

update_cms_entity_item.title: Update cms entity item
update_cms_entity_item.description: Change an item of a CMS entity: its name, status, or the value of any field, keyed by the field's unique_name.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

item.description: The fields to change: name, status (enabled or disabled), and any entity field keyed by its unique_name.

output.description: Update an entity item response data

delete_cms_entity_item.title: Delete cms entity item
delete_cms_entity_item.description: Permanently delete one item from a CMS entity.

env.description: Which copy of the bot to work on: `draft` (the editable version) or `draft,live` to apply to both the draft and the published bot. Omit for the provider default.

output.description: Delete an empty item response data

send_message.title: Send message
send_message.description: Send a message to one of the bot's Facebook Messenger users. The message uses BotStar's JSON message format, e.g. {text: 'Hello World'}; outside Messenger's 24-hour window a message_tag is required.

recipient.description: Who receives it: {id}, the Messenger user's id (the same id get_user takes).

message.description: The message in BotStar's JSON message format, e.g. {text: 'Hello World'}.

options.description: Send options: {message_tag}, one of CONFIRMED_EVENT_UPDATE, POST_PURCHASE_UPDATE, ACCOUNT_UPDATE, needed to message outside the 24-hour window.
